critical_evidence.evidence: No underside, trunk-floor or differential-mount photos, and no inspection report. The Carfax 'no structural damage reported' does not address diff-mount cracking. The car spent 2002–2015 in Colorado.

No record of water pump, thermostat, radiator or expansion tank replacement. The Carfax detail shows no service entries (no reported entry is not proof the work was not done). At 25 years old with long storage, original plastics are plausible.

documentation.rationale: The identity half is strong: the VIN matches the decode, the price is itemised, and a buyer-pulled Carfax shows 2 owners, consistent odometer readings and clean brands. The maintenance half is absent: no receipts, no cooling or rear-structure evidence, and no service entries on the report.

condition.rationale: Photos show glossy paint, straight panels, an intact beige top and clean wheels. The driver seat bolster shows creasing and wear. Nothing is shown of the underside, engine bay, tire dates or top rear window. Long low-use storage (~3,100 mi in 8.7 years) raises the odds of age-related seal, hose and tire issues.

price_value.rationale: $16,068 all-dealer-fee sits at the top of the $13,190–$16,642 fair-value range and about 16% above the $13,894 mid. That is in line with low-mile peers ($14,500–$15,991), but nothing about service or condition is proven to justify the premium.

mission_fit.rationale: A manual 2001 Z3 3.0i inside the ideal budget band is exactly the main bridge target and should resell easily in 6–24 months. Reliability is unproven until cooling and rear-structure questions are answered.

logistics.rationale: The car is in Fruitland Park, FL, 1,796 mi away. Independent BMW shops in the Orlando/Ocala area make a PPI arrangeable, but the dealer has not stated it permits one. A stock OBD-II 3.0i should be CA-smog feasible but must pass on arrival.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Manual 3.0i in dark green metallic over beige with a beige top and factory cross-spoke wheels, 2 owners and low miles: genuinely desirable spec. Sport Package fitment is unconfirmed.

evidence.mission_note: A manual 3.0i Z3 in the ideal budget band matches the enthusiast-bridge brief directly. Whether it is a reliable, resellable bridge depends on cooling and rear-structure evidence that the listing does not provide.
evidence.rationale: The listing and a buyer-pulled Carfax establish identity firmly. The VIN matches the decode, there are two personal owners (Colorado 2002–2015, then The Villages FL), odometer readings are consistent to 25,570 mi, and no accidents or title brands are reported. Jason has confirmed the manual gearbox. Photos show a straight, glossy dark-green roadster with an intact beige top and factory cross-spoke wheels; the only observed defect is wear on the driver seat bolster. Against that, the Carfax shows no service entries and only ~3,100 mi in the last 8.7 years, so age-related items (cooling plastics, seals, tires, fluids) are likely due and none are documented. Both model-critical items, rear structure and cooling history, are missing, and the Colorado years add an underbody-corrosion question. The $16,068 price sits at the top of the fair-value range and about 16% above its mid, without service evidence to support the premium.
evidence.next_action: Ask the dealer in writing to confirm an independent BMW-specialist PPI near Leesburg/Orlando, and to send tire DOT-code photos, underside and trunk-floor photos, a cold-start video and any service records before any deposit.
